docs.title: Mustfile
docs.text:
One config. Every language.

A polyglot build orchestrator with first-class support for 42 recipe types across 17+ languages.

Replace your Makefiles, Justfiles, and Taskfiles with a single Mustfile.toml that knows how to build, test, cache, and cross-compile every language in your project.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# Install
curl -fsSL https://github.com/anomalyco/mustfile/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

# Or with cargo
cargo install --locked mustfile

Create a Mustfile.toml:

[project]
name = "my-app"

[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

[recipe.test]
type    = "rust-test"
package = "my-app"
deps    = ["build"]

[recipe.lint]
type   = "shell"
script = "cargo clippy -- -D warnings"
phony  = true

Run:

must build      # builds the 'build' recipe
must test       # runs test + dependencies
must outdated   # shows what's stale
must explain build  # cache key, inputs, command preview

docs.title: Why must?
docs.text: Problem What must does mtime rebuilds break on branch switches Content-hashed caching for compiled recipes No language awareness — every build file reinvents toolchains First-class recipe types that know each toolchain Cross-compilation is manual and per-project Automatic target resolution + container opt-in Different commands per language (npm run, cargo build, go build) Consistent verbs: must build, must test, must lint Hard to introspect build state must list, must graph, must outdated, must explain

docs.title: Adding a new recipe type
docs.text:
1. Create the crate: crates/must-recipe-<lang>/
  2. Implement the Recipe trait from must-core:
use must_core::{BuildContext, CacheKey, Error, Recipe, RecipeOutput, Result};

pub struct MyBinRecipe {
    pub name: String,
    pub package: String,
    pub deps: Vec<String>,
    pub env: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl Recipe for MyBinRecipe {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn recipe_deps(&self) -> &[String] { &self.deps }

    fn execute(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<RecipeOutput> {
        let mut cmd = Command::new("my-tool");
        cmd.arg("build").arg(&self.package);
        cmd.current_dir(&ctx.project_root);
        // ... run command, return output
    }

    fn cache_key(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<CacheKey> { ... }
    fn inputs(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> { ... }
    fn outputs(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> { ... }
}
  1. Add the variant to RecipeType in must-config/src/schema.rs
  2. Wire it up in must-cli/src/main.rs (match arm in the recipe builder)
  3. Add tests — unit tests in the recipe crate, integration test in CLI
  4. Add docs — recipe page in site/docs/recipes/, entry in index
  5. Add an example in examples/

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
cargo test --workspace           # run all tests
cargo test -p must-recipe-rust   # test one crate
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings  # lint
cargo fmt --check                # format check

Writing tests: - Unit tests go in the same file under #[cfg(test)] mod tests - Real-execution tests should use match on Ok/ToolNotFound/RecipeFailed to handle missing toolchains - Cache tests use match pattern (not .unwrap()) to avoid flakes - Use tempfile::TempDir for filesystem tests

docs.text: must is organized as a Rust workspace with 26 crates, each with a single responsibility.

docs.title: Recipe trait
docs.text:
Every recipe implements this trait (defined in must-core):

trait Recipe {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn deps(&self) -> &[String];
    fn inputs(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>>;
    fn outputs(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>>;
    fn cache_strategy(&self) -> CacheStrategy;
    fn cache_key(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<CacheKey>;
    fn execute(&self, ctx: &BuildContext) -> Result<RecipeOutput>;
}

docs.title: BuildContext
docs.text:
Passed to every recipe execution:

struct BuildContext {
    project_root: PathBuf,
    cache_dir: PathBuf,
    log_dir: PathBuf,
    target: String,
    profile: String,
    env: HashMap<String, String>,
    dry_run: bool,
    parallelism: usize,
}

docs.title: CacheStrategy
docs.text:
enum CacheStrategy {
    Hash,    // content-hash of inputs
    Mtime,   // modification time
    Never,   // always re-run
}

docs.title: Execution flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI
    participant Engine
    participant Graph
    participant Cache

    CLI->>Engine: execute(recipes)
    Engine->>Graph: build DAG from recipes
    Graph-->>Engine: topological waves
    loop For each wave
        Engine->>Cache: check cache_key
        Cache-->>Engine: hit or miss
        alt Cache miss
            Engine->>Engine: execute recipe
            Engine->>Cache: store result
        end
    end
    Engine-->>CLI: ExecutionReport

docs.title: Dependency resolution
docs.text:
1. Parse Mustfile.toml → Config
  2. Build DAG from recipe deps
  3. Topological sort → waves of parallelizable recipes
  4. Each wave executes concurrently (bounded by parallelism)
  5. Cache check happens before each recipe execution

docs.title: Caching model
docs.text:
• Hash: SHA-256 of (recipe_name, type, input file contents, env, toolchain version, flags)
  • Mtime: Compare input file mtimes against last build
  • Never: Test recipes always re-run

Cache is stored on disk via sled embedded database in .mustfile/cache/.

docs.title: Cross-compilation
docs.text:
Target triples are resolved per-recipe:

  1. --target flag or [targets] group
  2. Per-recipe cross overrides (linker, container)
  3. Language-specific behavior (GOOS/GOARCH for Go, --target for Rust, cross-compiler for C)

docs.title: Importing from Makefile
docs.text: must can import existing Makefiles and generate a starter Mustfile.toml.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
must import Makefile

This reads your Makefile and generates:

  1. Mustfile.toml — converted recipes
  2. import-report.md — detailed report of what was converted and what needs manual review

docs.title: What gets imported
docs.text: Makefile construct Mustfile equivalent target: deps [recipe.target] with deps $(VAR) ${VAR} Recipe body script = "..." with type = "shell" .PHONY phony = true Pattern rules Skipped (needs manual conversion) Shell functions Preserved as-is in script Automatic variables ($@, $<, $^) Expanded inline

docs.title: Import report
docs.text:
The generated import-report.md contains:

  • Successfully converted recipes
  • Skipped rules (pattern rules, implicit rules)
  • Variables that need manual review
  • Suggestions for converting to first-class recipe types

Example:

# Import Report

## Converted (12 recipes)
- build → shell
- test → shell
- clean → shell (phony)
- lint → shell (phony)

## Needs review (3 items)
- `release` uses pattern rule — convert manually
- `deploy` calls SSH — may need secrets handling
- `CFLAGS` has complex expansion — verify

## Suggestions
- `build` compiles C code → consider `c-bin` type
- `test` runs pytest → consider `py-test` type

docs.title: Converting to first-class types
docs.text:
After import, consider upgrading shell recipes to first-class types:

# Before (imported)
[recipe.build]
type   = "shell"
script = "cargo build --release -p my-app"

# After (first-class)
[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

Benefits: automatic caching, cross-compilation support, toolchain version tracking.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: must uses intelligent caching to avoid redundant work. The strategy depends on the recipe type.

docs.title: Cache strategies
docs.text: Strategy Used by How it works hash rust-bin, go-bin, c-bin, ts-bin, etc. Content hash of inputs + env + toolchain version mtime shell (default) Modification time of input files never rust-test, go-test, py-test, etc. Always re-run (test results should be fresh)

docs.title: Content-hash caching
docs.text:
First-class recipe types (Rust, Go, C, TypeScript, etc.) use content-hashed caching:

  1. Compute a SHA-256 hash from: recipe name, type, input file contents, env vars, toolchain version, extra flags
  2. Look up the hash in the disk cache (.mustfile/cache/)
  3. If found → cache hit, skip execution
  4. If not found → execute, store the hash

This is branch-switch safe — switching branches changes file contents, which changes the hash.

docs.title: Cache key components
docs.text:
The hash is computed from:

  • Recipe name
  • Recipe type (e.g., rust-bin)
  • Input file contents (sorted by path, each file SHA-256'd)
  • Environment variables (sorted by key)
  • Toolchain ID (e.g., rustc 1.85.0)
  • Extra flags (profile, features, etc.)

docs.title: View cache key
docs.text:
must explain build

Shows the computed cache key and what went into it.

docs.title: mtime caching
docs.text:
Shell recipes default to mtime caching:

  1. Check if any input file's mtime is newer than the last build
  2. If newer → re-execute
  3. If not → cache hit

type   = "shell"
cache  = "hash"
inputs = ["proto/**/*.proto"]
script = "protoc --rust_out=src proto/*.proto"

docs.text:

docs.title: Mustfile.toml Reference
docs.text: The Mustfile.toml is the single source of truth for your project's build configuration.

docs.title: Top-level sections
docs.text:
[project]          # required — project metadata
[env]              # optional — global environment variables
[env.<profile>]    # optional — profile-specific overrides
[targets]          # optional — cross-compilation target groups
[recipe.<name>]    # required — one or more recipes
[include]          # optional — include other Mustfile.toml files

docs.title: [project]
docs.text:
[project]
name    = "my-app"       # required
version = "1.0.0"        # optional

docs.title: [env]
docs.text:
Environment variables available to all recipes. Supports variable interpolation.

[env]
OPT_LEVEL  = "2"
TARGET_DIR = "target/${TARGET}"    # ${VAR} expanded at runtime
REGISTRY   = "ghcr.io/myorg"

[env.release]
OPT_LEVEL = "3"

Resolution order (later wins):

  1. System environment
  2. [env] section
  3. [env.<profile>] section
  4. Recipe-level env field
  5. MUST_ARGS environment variable

docs.title: [targets]
docs.text:
Define named groups of compilation targets:

[targets]
default = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"]
release = [
    "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
    "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu",
    "x86_64-apple-darwin",
]

Use with --target:

must build --target release
must build --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

docs.title: [recipe.<name>]
docs.text:
Every recipe has these fields:

Field Type Description type string Required. One of the 41 recipe type identifiers package string Package/target/module path (most types) script string Shell command (shell / npm types) script_win string Windows override for script (shorthand) scripts map Per-OS script overrides. Keys: macos, linux, freebsd, netbsd, openbsd, win, unix, bsd. Takes priority over script_win and script. deps string[] Dependencies — must complete before this recipe env map Recipe-specific environment variables inputs string[] Input file globs (for cache hashing) outputs string[] Output file paths phony bool Always re-run, skip caching (default: false) cache string "hash", "mtime", or "never" workdir string Working directory relative to project root features string[] Feature flags (Rust recipes) image string Docker image name (Docker recipes) dockerfile string Path to Dockerfile build_args map Docker build args plugin string Plugin name (plugin type) sources string[] Source files (C recipes) includes string[] Include directories (C recipes) link_libs string[] Libraries to link (C recipes) ldflags string Linker flags (Go recipes)

[recipe.cli.cross]
"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" = {}
"aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" = { linker = "aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc" }

docs.title: Layered environments
docs.text:
Environment variables are resolved in layers, with later layers overriding earlier ones:

system env → [env] → [env.<profile>] → recipe.env → MUST_ARGS

Use MUST_ARGS to pass extra args from CI:

MUST_ARGS="--release" must build

docs.title: Cross-Compilation
docs.text: must supports cross-compilation with automatic toolchain resolution.

docs.title: Defining targets
docs.text:
[targets]
default = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"]
release = [
    "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
    "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu",
    "x86_64-apple-darwin",
    "aarch64-apple-darwin",
]

docs.title: Building for a target
docs.text:
must build --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
must build --target release   # builds all targets in the group

docs.title: Per-recipe cross-compilation config
docs.text:
Override linker, toolchain, or container settings per target:

[recipe.cli]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "cli"

[recipe.cli.cross]
"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" = {}
"aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" = { linker = "aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc" }
"x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" = { cross = "container" }

docs.title: Cross-compilation fields
docs.text: Field Description linker Custom linker for this target cross "container" to use cross-rs Docker containers ar Custom archiver sysroot Custom sysroot path

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
• Uses cargo build --target <triple>
  • Supports cross-rs containers via cross = "container"
  • Automatic linker configuration from target triple

docs.title: Go
docs.text:
• Sets GOOS and GOARCH from the target triple
  • Supports all standard Go cross-compilation targets

docs.title: C/C++
docs.text:
• Uses the target triple to select a cross-compiler
  • Example: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu → aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc

docs.title: Target triple format
docs.text:
must uses LLVM target triples:

<arch>-<vendor>-<os>-<abi>

Common triples:

Triple Platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu Linux x86_64 aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu Linux ARM64 x86_64-apple-darwin macOS Intel aarch64-apple-darwin macOS Apple Silicon x86_64-pc-windows-msvc Windows x86_64

docs.title: Cross-Platform Recipes
docs.text: Mustfile supports writing shell recipes that work across macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows. On Unix systems recipes use sh -c. On Windows they use cmd /C.

docs.title: Quick: Windows override
docs.text:
Use script for the default and script_win for Windows:

[recipe.clean]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script     = "rm -rf build"
script_win = "rmdir /s /q build"

docs.title: Per-OS scripts
docs.text:
For finer control, use the scripts table to override per operating system:

[recipe.build]
type   = "shell"
script = "make"

[recipe.build.scripts]
macos   = "make -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
linux   = "make -j$(nproc)"
freebsd = "gmake -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"
win     = "nmake"

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
The scripts table is checked in order of specificity. The first match wins:

Platform Checked in order macOS scripts.macos → scripts.unix → script Linux scripts.linux → scripts.unix → script FreeBSD scripts.freebsd → scripts.bsd → scripts.unix → script NetBSD / OpenBSD scripts.netbsd / scripts.openbsd → scripts.bsd → scripts.unix → script Windows scripts.win → script_win → script

The scripts table takes priority over script_win and script.

docs.title: Available keys
docs.text: Key Matches macos macOS only linux Linux only freebsd FreeBSD only netbsd NetBSD only openbsd OpenBSD only win Windows only unix Any Unix (macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, ...) bsd FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my-app"
version = "1.0.0"

[recipe.build]
type    = "shell"
cache   = "hash"
inputs  = ["src/**/*.c"]
outputs = ["build/app"]
script  = "mkdir -p build && cc -o build/app src/main.c"

[recipe.build.scripts]
macos   = "mkdir -p build && cc -o build/app src/main.c"
linux   = "mkdir -p build && gcc -o build/app src/main.c"
freebsd = "mkdir -p build && clang -o build/app src/main.c"
win     = "if not exist build mkdir build && cl /Fe:build/app.exe src/main.c"

[recipe.clean]
type  = "shell"
phony = true

[recipe.clean.scripts]
macos   = "rm -rf build"
linux   = "rm -rf build"
freebsd = "rm -rf build"
win     = "rmdir /s /q build"

[recipe.test]
type   = "shell"
deps   = ["build"]
phony  = true
script = "./build/app --test"

[recipe.test.scripts]
win = "build\\app.exe --test"

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Path separators: Use / in Unix scripts, \\ in Windows scripts.
  • Environment variables: $VAR in sh, %VAR% in cmd.
  • Language recipes don't need this: Recipes like rust-bin, go-bin, py-bin etc. invoke language-specific tools that are already cross-platform. Only shell and npm recipes typically need platform overrides.
  • CI: Test Windows scripts on a Windows runner alongside your Unix runners.
  • Fallback: Always set script as the default — it's used when no platform matches.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Extend must with Lua scripts. Plugins have access to shell execution, file I/O, glob, environment variables, and logging.

docs.title: Plugin location
docs.text:
Place .lua files in .mustfile/plugins/:

.mustfile/
  plugins/
    protoc.lua
    codegen.lua

docs.title: Using a plugin
docs.text:
[recipe.codegen]
type   = "plugin"
plugin = "protoc"    # matches protoc.lua

docs.title: Plugin structure
docs.text:
A plugin must define an execute function:

function execute(ctx)
    -- ctx.profile: current profile name
    -- ctx.target: current target triple
    -- ctx.project_root: project root path
    -- ctx.env: table of environment variables

    return {
        stdout = "output message",
        stderr = "",
        success = true,
    }
end

docs.title: deps()
docs.text:
Declare dependencies:

function deps()
    return { "build", "codegen" }
end

docs.title: inputs(ctx)
docs.text:
Return input file paths for caching:

function inputs(ctx)
    return { "proto/service.proto", "proto/types.proto" }
end

docs.title: outputs(ctx)
docs.text:
Return output file paths:

function outputs(ctx)
    return { "src/proto/mod.rs" }
end

docs.title: cache_key(ctx)
docs.text:
Custom cache key (default: script content hash):

function cache_key(ctx)
    return "custom-" .. ctx.profile
end

docs.title: Built-in stdlib
docs.text: Function Signature Description shell_exec shell_exec(cmd) → table Execute shell command. Returns {success, exit_code, stdout, stderr} read_file read_file(path) → string Read file contents write_file write_file(path, content) Write to file file_exists file_exists(path) → bool Check if file exists mkdir mkdir(path) Create directory (recursive) glob glob(pattern) → table Match file paths (returns 1-indexed table) env_get env_get(key) → string? Get environment variable set_env set_env(key, value) Set environment variable log_info log_info(msg) Log info message log_warn log_warn(msg) Log warning

docs.title: Example: Protocol buffer codegen
docs.text:
-- .mustfile/plugins/protoc.lua

function inputs(ctx)
    return glob(ctx.project_root .. "/proto/*.proto")
end

function outputs(ctx)
    return { "src/proto/mod.rs", "src/proto/types.rs" }
end

function execute(ctx)
    local protos = glob(ctx.project_root .. "/proto/*.proto")
    local count = 0

    for _, p in ipairs(protos) do
        local result = shell_exec("protoc --rust_out=src/proto " .. p)
        if not result.success then
            return {
                stdout = "",
                stderr = "protoc failed: " .. result.stderr,
                success = false,
            }
        end
        count = count + 1
    end

    return {
        stdout = "generated " .. count .. " proto files",
        stderr = "",
        success = true,
    }
end

docs.text:
must plugin list              # list discovered plugins
must plugin check protoc      # validate a plugin
must plugin install <URL>     # install from URL

docs.title: Environment variable layers
docs.text:
Environment variables are resolved in layers. Later layers override earlier ones:

1. System environment
2. [env] section in Mustfile.toml
3. [env.<profile>] section
4. Recipe-level env field
5. MUST_ARGS environment variable

docs.title: Global environment
docs.text:
[env]
LOG_LEVEL = "info"
OPT_LEVEL = "2"
REGISTRY  = "ghcr.io/myorg"

docs.title: Profile overrides
docs.text:
[env]
OPT_LEVEL = "2"

[env.release]
OPT_LEVEL = "3"
LOG_LEVEL = "warn"

Select a profile:

must build --profile release

docs.title: Recipe-level environment
docs.text:
[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

[recipe.build.env]
RUSTFLAGS = "-C target-cpu=native"

docs.title: Variable interpolation
docs.text:
Use ${VAR} syntax for runtime expansion:

[env]
TARGET_DIR = "target/${TARGET}"
IMAGE_TAG  = "${REGISTRY}/api:${VERSION}"

$VAR and ${VAR} are both supported. Undefined variables expand to empty strings.

docs.title: MUST_ARGS
docs.text:
Pass extra flags from CI or wrappers:

MUST_ARGS="--release --fail-fast" must build

docs.title: Shell environment inheritance
docs.text:
Recipes inherit the full system environment plus all must-configured variables. This means:

  • PATH is available by default
  • Any env var set in CI (GitHub Actions, etc.) is accessible
  • must env vars are layered on top, not replacements

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and how to resolve them.

docs.title: must doctor — Start here
docs.text:
Run must doctor to check which toolchains are installed and get installation hints:

must doctor — environment health check

  ✓ cargo         1.78.0
  ✗ go (optional) Install from https://go.dev/dl/
  ✓ cc/gcc        Apple clang 15.0
  ✗ tsc (optional) npm install -g typescript
  ...

Items marked (optional) are only needed for recipe types that use them.

docs.title: unknown recipe 'name'
docs.text:
You referenced a recipe name that doesn't exist in your Mustfile.toml.

Fix: Check spelling and run must list to see all available recipes.

docs.title: cycle detected in recipe graph: a → b → a
docs.text:
Two or more recipes form a circular dependency.

Fix: Remove one of the deps entries that creates the cycle.

docs.title: recipe 'name' failed with exit code 1
docs.text:
The recipe's command returned a non-zero exit code.

Fix: 1. Run must log <name> to see the full output 2. Run the command directly in your shell to reproduce 3. Check working directory — recipes run in the project root (where Mustfile.toml lives)

docs.title: tool not found: cargo
docs.text:
The required toolchain is not installed or not on PATH.

Fix: Install the tool and verify with must doctor. Common installations:

Tool Install cargo rustup.rs go go.dev/dl cc / gcc Xcode CLI tools (macOS), build-essential (Linux) tsc npm install -g typescript biome npm install -g @biomejs/biome python3 python.org or brew install python uv docs.astral.sh/uv zig ziglang.org docker docker.com swift Xcode (macOS) or swift.org dotnet dot.net dart dart.dev nim choosenim or nim-lang.org elixir / mix elixir-lang.org flutter flutter.dev gradle Build scan or gradle.org bundle / ruby ruby-lang.org

docs.title: toolchain not found for target 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'
docs.text:
Cross-compilation target requires a specific linker or toolchain.

Fix: 1. Install the cross-compilation toolchain (e.g., apt install gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu) 2. Configure the linker in your Mustfile:

[recipe.build.cross]
"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" = { linker = "x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc" }

Or use container-based cross-compilation:

[recipe.build.cross]
"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" = { cross = "container" }

docs.title: config error in Mustfile.toml: ...
docs.text:
TOML parsing or validation error.

Fix: Check the error message for the specific issue. Common causes: - Missing type field on a recipe - Invalid recipe type name - Missing required field (e.g., package for rust-bin)

docs.title: Recipe always re-runs (never caches)
docs.text: Check: - Is phony = true set? This forces re-execution every time. - Is cache = "never" set? - For mtime caching: do your outputs exist? If outputs are missing, the recipe always re-runs.

docs.title: Cache is stale after switching branches
docs.text:
Hash-based caching is branch-switch safe because it uses content hashes. If you're using mtime caching, branch switches can cause false rebuilds because file timestamps change.

Fix: Use cache = "hash" for expensive recipes:

[recipe.build]
type   = "shell"
cache  = "hash"
inputs = ["src/**/*.rs"]
script = "cargo build"

docs.title: Clearing cache
docs.text:
must cache invalidate build     # clear one recipe
must cache invalidate --all     # clear everything
must clean --cache              # remove outputs + cache

docs.title: Builds are slow
docs.text:
1. Use parallelism: must build -j4 (default is number of CPUs)
  2. Check cache hits: must outdated shows which recipes are fresh vs stale
  3. Use hash caching for expensive shell recipes (codegen, protoc, etc.)

docs.title: must itself is slow to start
docs.text: The must binary is a single compiled Rust binary. If startup is slow, check: - Disk I/O on the cache directory (.mustfile/cache/) - Number of input file globs being expanded

docs.title: must watch doesn't detect changes
docs.text: The watcher uses notify which relies on OS file system events. Known limitations: - NFS mounts and some CI environments don't emit events - Very large directories may have delayed detection - On macOS, FSEvents has a latency of a few seconds

docs.title: Watch mode
docs.text:
Automatically rebuild when files change:

must watch             # watch and rebuild on changes
must watch build test  # watch specific recipes

must uses filesystem watchers (via notify crate) to detect changes. When a change is detected:

  1. Debounce for 200ms (avoid thrashing on multi-file saves)
  2. Rebuild all watched recipes
  3. Print results
  4. Wait for next change

Press Ctrl+C to stop.

docs.title: Build logs
docs.text: must stores build output for each recipe execution.

docs.title: View a log
docs.text:
must log build          # show last build output for "build"
must log test           # show last test output

docs.title: Follow in real time
docs.text:
must log build --follow

Streams new output as it arrives (like tail -f).

docs.title: List all logs
docs.text:
must log

Output:

NAME         SIZE
build        1.2 KB
test         4.5 KB
lint         256 B

docs.title: Clear logs
docs.text: must log --clear

docs.title: Log location
docs.text:
Logs are stored in .mustfile/logs/ as <recipe-name>.log files.

Add to .gitignore:

.mustfile/

docs.title: Migrating from Just
docs.text: just is a command runner with a Make-like syntax. must provides a superset of just's functionality with language-aware recipes.

docs.title: Concept mapping
docs.text: just must justfile Mustfile.toml recipe_name: [recipe.recipe_name] Recipe body (indented) script = "..." recipe_name: dep1 dep2 deps = ["dep1", "dep2"] export VAR := "value" [env] VAR = "value" {{ VAR }} ${VAR} [private] No direct equivalent — omit from Mustfile [unix] / [windows] Use shell conditionals or separate recipes just --list must list just --dry-run must --dry-run just --watch must watch just recipe_name must build recipe_name

docs.title: Side-by-side
docs.text:
justfile:

export OPT_LEVEL := "2"

build:
    cargo build --release

test: build
    cargo test

lint:
    cargo clippy -- -D warnings

clean:
    cargo clean

Mustfile.toml:

[project]
name = "my-app"

[env]
OPT_LEVEL = "2"

[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

[recipe.test]
type    = "rust-test"
package = "my-app"
deps    = ["build"]

[recipe.lint]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script = "cargo clippy -- -D warnings"

[recipe.clean]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script = "cargo clean"

docs.title: Key differences
docs.text: Feature just must Language awareness No — all recipes are shell Yes — 41 first-class recipe types Caching No built-in caching Hash/mtime/never per recipe Cross-compilation Manual Automatic with target groups Dependency graph Flat DAG with parallel waves Plugins No Lua plugins with stdlib Build logs No Per-recipe log storage Outdated checking No must outdated

docs.title: Migration steps
docs.text:
1. Rename justfile to Mustfile.toml
  2. Wrap each recipe in [recipe.<name>] with type = "shell"
  3. Move exports to [env] section
  4. Convert {{ VAR }} to ${VAR}
  5. Upgrade shell recipes to first-class types where possible

docs.title: Migrating from Make
docs.text: A practical guide to converting Makefiles to Mustfile.toml.

docs.title: Concept mapping
docs.text: Make must Makefile Mustfile.toml target: deps [recipe.target] with deps Recipe body (tab-indented) script = "..." $(VAR) / ${VAR} ${VAR} (same syntax) .PHONY: clean phony = true $(MAKE) -C subdir workdir = "subdir/" ifeq / ifdef [env.<profile>] or recipe-level env include other.mk [include] paths = [...] @echo "message" script = "echo 'message'" Pattern rules (%.o: %.c) No equivalent — use a loop or first-class type $(shell ...) Use must's built-in variable expansion $@, $<, $^ Expanded inline during import

docs.title: 1. Import
docs.text:
must import Makefile

This generates Mustfile.toml and import-report.md.

docs.title: 2. Review the import report
docs.text:
Check for:

  • Pattern rules that need manual conversion
  • Complex variable expansions
  • Implicit dependencies

docs.title: 3. Convert to first-class types
docs.text:
Replace generic shell recipes with language-specific types:

# Before
[recipe.build]
type   = "shell"
script = "cargo build --release -p my-app"

# After
[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

docs.title: 4. Move variables to [env]
docs.text:
# Makefile
CFLAGS := -O2 -Wall
TARGET := my-app

# Mustfile.toml
[env]
CFLAGS = "-O2 -Wall"
TARGET = "my-app"

docs.title: 5. Convert phony targets
docs.text:
# Makefile
.PHONY: clean test
clean:
    rm -rf build/
test:
    cargo test

# Mustfile.toml
[recipe.clean]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script = "rm -rf build/"

[recipe.test]
type    = "rust-test"
package = "my-app"

docs.title: 6. Remove tab indentation
docs.text: must uses TOML strings — no tab-significant whitespace.

docs.title: Side-by-side comparison
docs.text:
Makefile:

CFLAGS := -O2 -Wall
SRC    := $(wildcard src/*.c)
OBJ    := $(SRC:.c=.o)

my-app: $(OBJ)
    $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^

%.o: %.c
    $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

.PHONY: clean test
test: my-app
    ./my-app --test

clean:
    rm -f $(OBJ) my-app

Mustfile.toml:

[project]
name = "my-app"

[env]
CFLAGS = "-O2 -Wall"

[recipe.build]
type    = "c-bin"
sources = ["src/*.c"]
includes = ["src/"]

[recipe.test]
type   = "shell"
deps   = ["build"]
phony  = true
script = "./my-app --test"

[recipe.clean]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script = "rm -f src/*.o my-app"

docs.title: Migrating from Taskfile
docs.text: Taskfile is a YAML-based task runner. must uses TOML and provides language-aware recipes.

docs.title: Concept mapping
docs.text: Taskfile must Taskfile.yml Mustfile.toml tasks: [recipe.<name>] sections cmds: script = "..." deps: deps = [...] env: [env] or recipe-level env sources: inputs generates: outputs status: Automatic via cache strategy dir: workdir task --list must list task --dry must --dry-run task --watch must watch

docs.title: Side-by-side
docs.text:
Taskfile.yml:

version: '3'

env:
  OPT_LEVEL: "2"

tasks:
  build:
    cmds:
      - cargo build --release -p my-app
    sources:
      - src/**/*.rs
    generates:
      - target/release/my-app

  test:
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - cargo test -p my-app

  lint:
    cmds:
      - cargo clippy -- -D warnings

Mustfile.toml:

[project]
name = "my-app"

[env]
OPT_LEVEL = "2"

[recipe.build]
type    = "rust-bin"
package = "my-app"

[recipe.test]
type    = "rust-test"
package = "my-app"
deps    = ["build"]

[recipe.lint]
type   = "shell"
phony  = true
script = "cargo clippy -- -D warnings"

docs.title: Key differences
docs.text: Feature Taskfile must Config format YAML TOML Language awareness No 41 first-class recipe types Caching sources/generates with status check Automatic hash/mtime/never Cross-compilation Manual env vars Target groups + auto toolchain Parallel execution Yes Yes (DAG waves) Plugins No Lua plugins

docs.title: Migration steps
docs.text:
1. Convert YAML to TOML syntax
  2. Wrap each task in [recipe.<name>]
  3. Move cmds to script (join multi-cmd with &&)
  4. Move deps directly
  5. Replace sources/generates with appropriate cache strategy
  6. Upgrade to first-class recipe types where possible

docs.title: Precompiled Binaries
docs.text: The precompiled-bin recipe type downloads prebuilt binaries and caches them with SHA-256 verification.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
• Downloading tools your project depends on (e.g., protoc, buf, dart-sass)
  • Pinning CLI versions across your team
  • Avoiding system-level installs in CI

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
[recipe.protoc]
type   = "precompiled-bin"
url    = "https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v28.0/protoc-28.0-linux-x86_64.zip"
sha256 = "abc123..."
output = "bin/protoc"

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description url string Yes HTTPS URL to download sha256 string Recommended Expected SHA-256 hex digest output string Yes Output path relative to project root

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• HTTPS only — http:// URLs are rejected
  • Path traversal protection — output cannot contain ..
  • SHA-256 verification — streamed chunked verification before finalizing the file

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Downloads to a .tmp file using streaming I/O (low memory usage)
  2. Verifies SHA-256 digest against sha256 field (chunked, O(1) heap)
  3. Atomically renames .tmp to the final output path
  4. On cache hit, skips download entirely

docs.title: Example: multiple tools
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my-app"
version = "0.1.0"

[recipe.protoc]
type   = "precompiled-bin"
url    = "https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v28.0/protoc-28.0-linux-x86_64.zip"
sha256 = "abc123..."
output = ".tools/protoc"

[recipe.buf]
type   = "precompiled-bin"
url    = "https://github.com/bufbuild/buf/releases/download/v1.40.0/buf-Linux-x86_64"
sha256 = "def456..."
output = ".tools/buf"

[recipe.generate]
type    = "shell"
deps    = ["protoc"]
inputs  = ["proto/*.proto"]
outputs = ["src/generated/*.rs"]
script  = "protoc --rust_out=src proto/*.proto"

docs.text:
[recipe.build]
type    = "swift-bin"
package = "."

Runs: swift build -c release (in package directory)

Cache key includes: swift --version, package, env vars.

docs.title: swift-test — Run tests
docs.text:
[recipe.test]
type    = "swift-test"
package = "."
deps    = ["build"]

Runs: swift test (in package directory)

Cache strategy: never (test results should always be fresh).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Applies to Description package string all Package directory path (default .) deps string[] all Dependencies env map all Environment variables

All recipes also support these common fields: deps, env, cache ("hash" / "mtime" / "never"), phony (always re-run), and workdir (working directory).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my-swift-project"

[recipe.build]
type    = "swift-bin"
package = "."

[recipe.test]
type    = "swift-test"
package = "."
deps    = ["build"]

docs.title: TypeScript Recipes
docs.text: must provides four TypeScript recipe types: ts-bin, ts-check, ts-lint, and npm.

docs.title: ts-bin — Compile TypeScript
docs.text:
[recipe.build]
type    = "ts-bin"
package = "tsconfig.json"

Runs: tsc --project tsconfig.json

Cache key includes: package, env vars.

docs.title: ts-check — Type-check only
docs.text:
[recipe.typecheck]
type    = "ts-check"
package = "tsconfig.json"

Runs: tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json

Cache strategy: never (type-check results should always be fresh).

docs.title: ts-lint — Lint with Biome
docs.text:
[recipe.lint]
type    = "ts-lint"
package = "src/"

Runs: biome check src/

Cache strategy: never (lint results should always be fresh).

docs.title: npm — Run an npm script
docs.text:
[recipe.bundle]
type       = "npm"
npm_script = "build"
workdir    = "packages/api"

Runs: npm run build (in packages/api)

Cache strategy: never (npm scripts are not cached).

docs.text:

All recipes also support these common fields: deps, env, cache ("hash" / "mtime" / "never"), phony (always re-run), and workdir (working directory).
